analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a head-side paragraph near lines 173-181 describing four test names. Two cover OpenRouter returned-reasoning tool turns and two replay captured OpenRouter strict weather-tool requests, with tool choice omitted, auto and none, plus a five-step conversation. No runtime code, configuration, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache or authorization behavior changes. The base units I examined were the complete existing document, including SSD cache test guidance, which matches T-041's description. Relevant threat IDs (T-041, TB-002, TB-007) do not change. The new text asserts that captured requests are 'held byte for byte and hash-checked'. This is a fixture-integrity statement, not a control. The new text describes no secrets, credentials or production endpoints, and the added tests run on the local coordinator and HTTP paths. I could not verify the named tests or fixtures, which are outside the supplied evidence. Unverified contracts: whether captured OpenRouter fixtures contain any sensitive data, and whether the tests actually exist. Neither is evidence of a regression, so I made no finding. No threat-model update is needed for this documentation-only change.
